title: P0 hosted API cross-region KV-cache invalidation postmortem
content:
Summary:
During a planned rollout of a KV-cache schema change, an invalidation job ran without the intended region-scoping filter and triggered synchronous global cache invalidation across all hosted-api regions. Within ~90s of the invalidation job starting, we observed a sharp increase in request p95/p99 latency and a wave of 5xx errors for streaming and non-streaming calls as backends hit CPU/GPU memory pressure from cache-warm storms and connection churn. The incident lasted ~2h20m from detection to final mitigations.

Impact:
- Time window: 2026-10-18 15:07 UTC -> 2026-10-18 17:27 UTC (mitigations engaged; follow-ups continued)
- Affected surface: hosted API production across eu-west-1, us-east-1, us-west-2, ap-southeast-1
- User impact: elevated generation latencies (p99 up to 8.9s), intermittent 5xx (up to 12% of requests) and streaming session drops for customers with medium-high concurrency patterns. Some Dedicated customers experienced degraded throughput because warm-up traffic contaminated shared warmers.
- Business: Several customer support tickets and automated alerts; no SLA credit assessment yet pending billing analytics.

What happened (root cause and contributing factors):
Root cause: A cache invalidation orchestrator job (infra/ops tool) was updated to support a new schema validation and a small change inadvertently removed the region filter predicate. The job iterated over all cache partitions and issued an invalidation marker globally. This caused simultaneous cold-cache behavior across regions.

Contributing factors:
- Canary scope: canary run used control data that did not exercise the region filter path, so the missing filter was not observed in preflight.
- Lack of circuit-breaker: the invalidation job had no rate-limiting nor a backoff to avoid thundering-warmers hits to origin services.
- Warmers design assumption: warmers assumed incremental invalidations; global cold starts caused many warmers to synchronously request heavy KV payloads, leading to resource contention (CPU, memory, GPU cache thrash).
- Monitoring blindspot: our cross-region dependency dashboard does not clearly surface coordinated cache turnovers as an aggregated signal; we had region-level graphs but no global 'simultaneous invalidation' alert.
- Rollout controls: the job was allowed to run across regions by default; there was no enforced per-region opt-in gate.

Detection and response timeline (high level):
- 15:05 UTC: Scheduled maintenance window began; ops started rollout of schema change.
- 15:07 UTC: First anomalous p95 latency spike in eu-west-1 (alert threshold breached).
- 15:08 - 15:10 UTC: SRE on-call (Aaron) begins investigation; notices correlation between invalidation job and latency by scanning recent jobs.
- 15:12 UTC: Error spikes propagate to us-east-1 and us-west-2; streaming sessions start to drop. Pager duty escalates to P0.
- 15:15 UTC: Emergency mitigation: paused the invalidation orchestrator; however job had already issued invalidation markers for all regions.
- 15:20 UTC: Temporary throttle applied at edge to slow down rewarmers (rate-limit prefix). This reduced immediate load on origin but did not fully restore steady state.
- 15:40 UTC: Re-enabled prioritized warmers only (customers with active sessions) and disabled bulk warmers. Observed partial recovery of p50/p95.
- 16:05 UTC: Rolled back the schema change and redeployed orchestrator with a soft-fail region filter (defensive check) — note: rollback took time to take effect due to running processes.
- 16:40 UTC: Added global circuit-breaker to the invalidation path and introduced randomized rewarm jitter to warmers.  Errors and latencies gradually declined.
- 17:27 UTC: Alert noise returned to baseline; customer support triage completed initial responses.

Mitigations performed (immediate):
- Paused and cancelled remaining invalidation tasks; reverted the orchestration change to prior commit.
- Applied edge-level rate limits to rewarm requests to origins to dampen immediate traffic surges.
- Disabled non-essential warmers (bulk warmers) and prioritized active session warmers.
- Deployed short-term config that enforces per-region execution for critical maintenance jobs.

Post-incident analysis (what we learned):
- Global ops jobs need explicit region scoping and platform-level enforcement; a small change can have global blast radius.
- Warmers must be resilient to global cold starts: they should ramp with exponential backoff, randomized jitter, and a global token bucket to prevent simultaneous bursts.
- Canary testing must include negative-paths and gating checks for region-scoped logic. Our canary data set and checks were insufficient.
- Observability: we need an aggregated signal that detects concurrent cache turnover across multiple regions and converts that into a high-priority alert.

Action items (owners and proposed due dates):
1) Enforce region-scoped job execution at the control plane level (infra). Owner: Aaron Chen. Due: 2026-11-05.
2) Add a mandatory preflight validator that fails CI for orchestrator jobs lacking explicit region scoping and run it in infra CI. Owner: Priya Desai. Due: 2026-10-30.
3) Redesign warmers to support token-bucket throttling, per-region ramp-up, randomized jitter, and persistent progress markers. Owner: Michael O'Neill (serving-runtime). Due: 2026-12-15.
4) Implement a global "simultaneous-invalidation" detector in SRE monitoring; alert if >2 regions see cache invalidation marker within X seconds and associated spike in origin QPS. Owner: Jules Kim. Due: 2026-11-12.
5) Update runbooks: add explicit steps for immediate edge-level throttling, how to identify invalidation-origin jobs, and rollback checklist. Owner: Sofia Martinez. Due: 2026-10-28.
6) Postmortem review with product and solutions engineering to evaluate whether Dedicated customers need isolated warmers or configured warm-up SLAs. Owner: Product-Hosted-API liaison (TBD). Due: 2026-11-01.

Runbook draft notes (quick additions to SRE runbook):
- Detection: check invalidation job logs for missing region parameter; query job-run metadata for scope flags.
- Immediate mitigation steps: pause invalidation job, enable edge-rate limit (approx 500 rps global for warmers), disable bulk warmers, enable prioritized warmers.
- Longer mitigation: rollback orchestrator code, redeploy with defensive checks, reintroduce per-region gating.
- Post-mitigation validation: monitor p95/p99, 5xx rate, streaming reconnect rate, and origin CPU/GPU memory. Keep elevated monitoring for 48h.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Why did the canary dataset fail to catch the missing predicate? (action: expand canary to include region filter negative tests)
- Are there existing warmers deployed in Dedicated that share infrastructure with hosted API warmers? Need confirmation from solutions-engineering.
- Billing/SLA follow-up: quantify customer exposure for SLA credit decision.

Appendix (artifacts and quick pointers):
- Orchestrator job run IDs: infra-job-20261018-1459 (main), infra-job-20261018-1504 (cancelled)
- Key logs: s3://infra-logs/invalidator/2026/10/18/infra-job-20261018-1459.log
- Alerts: alert-ids: A-38912 (eu-west-1 p95), A-38917 (us-east-1 streaming-errors)
- Related PRs and CI: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1897 (change that removed region filter), https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-warmers/pull/412 (warming throttles prototype)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working postmortem; owners/timelines proposed above are negotiable.
- The runbook additions are intentionally conservative — the immediate objective is to reduce blast radius from global ops jobs.
- We should discuss separating warmers infra for Dedicated vs Hosted in the postmortem review meeting.

Prepared by: Sofia Martinez (SRE)
Reviewers: Aaron Chen, Priya Desai, Michael O'Neill, Jules Kim
Status: in_review
